title: RC-17 duplicate module instance: the nonce authority is plain module state with no duplicate-load guard, so a second copy of the module (path casing, ESM/CJS dual load, a cleared require cache) is a second, independent lock for the same wallet

evidence.note: const chains = new Map<string, Promise<unknown>>(): module-scope state; a second evaluation of the module creates a second, empty Map
serialization holds only among callers that share the same Map instance
no output: no duplicate-load guard and no globalThis registry anywhere at the base SHA

production importers are exactly bot.ts:77 and exitEngine.ts:12, both "./utils/nonceAuthority" from src/, so the two production imports resolve to one file and one instance today; tests reload it on purpose (vi.importActual / dynamic import after vi.resetModules)

forceConsistentCasingInFileNames is absent from both (present only in tsconfig.json), so a differently cased import would compile under the bot config; on Windows (this operator) a differently cased specifier loads a second module instance under CommonJS

sibling_sites_checked: The other module-state singletons named by RC-17 (sell lock exitManager.ts:14/:53/:104, ExitWorker exitEngine.ts:1421, anti-rug registry detector.ts:192/:197/:247) are in the EXIT and ANTIRUG slices; their slices own those entries. In this slice the only lock/registry singleton is nonceAuthority.ts:43; provider.ts:7-8 caches providers in module Maps, where a duplicate instance means a second provider, not a capital defect.
severity_rationale: S1, equal to the research suggestion ("latent S1"). The gap (no guard) is confirmed at the base SHA; a duplicate load does not happen with the two production imports today, so the condition is a non-default load (a differently cased import, the planned ESM conversion in Phase 26, a test-style module reset in a tool). When it happens two buys/sells of one wallet can sign the same nonce at once: a replaced or double-spent transaction. Mitigation: the duplicate-load guard rail of plan 22-12 (D-05) closes it; status stays confirmed until the 22-29 re-audit verifies that rail, as the PROTOCOL lifecycle allows no other change here.
recommendation: Mitigated by the planned rail 22-12 (Symbol.for registry with an epoch sentinel, D-05) and forceConsistentCasingInFileNames in all tsconfigs; 22-29 re-audits the diff of nonceAuthority.ts and moves this entry forward only on evidence. No further behaviour decision.

sub_claims.claim: No duplicate-load guard exists for the nonce authority at the base SHA
A duplicate load occurs in the production import graph at the base SHA

status_note: The re-audit reviewed src/guards/singleton.ts and all four registrations in full: the guard throws before the guarded state exists, and casing, junction and cache aliases converge on one registry entry. Moved to fixed on that evidence; the Phase 26 ESM conversion must re-check it (AUD-REAUDIT-002).
